answer: We formulate a mechanism comprising dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices, which guarantees strict Nash equilibrium against Sybil multiplication. An agent's expected payoff from multiplying identities is diminished as the tide of penalties rises with each additional Sybil instance, rendering such actions irrational. The marble of trust is thus preserved as agents converge on honest strategies. In the zenith of equilibrium, no agent can improve payoff by unilaterally deviating, thereby ensuring Sybil resistance.
